structured_plan.G: Pending research. Integrate only changes that pass the independent FP64 oracle and preserve the ABI, full output overwrite, arbitrary-size correctness, and caller thread budget. Benchmark the integrated program and independently confirm it before selecting the final candidate.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline uses r-c-k accumulation, does not use the supplied thread budget, and falls back to the generic loop for the timed sizes. Cache locality, explicit SIMD, and thread scaling are distinct high-potential opportunities; a fourth tree would likely duplicate one of these. The supplied baseline is valid, with mean time 0.13384 seconds and score 0.5, but its three samples are not broken down by size or thread budget. Require each tree to test all valid sizes for correctness and assess performance under the official timed sizes and thread budgets; do not assume individual gains will combine.

children.objective: Explore a single-thread, cache-friendly row-major GEMM using loop interchange and cache blocking, with tile sizes that work across arbitrary n and correct handling of edge tiles. Keep this branch free of explicit SIMD intrinsics, panel packing, and OpenMP so it isolates locality and compiler auto-vectorization. Ensure every output element is assigned on every call, validate against the FP64 oracle for all supported sizes, and compare official timings at both timed sizes with one thread.
children.subject: Single-thread cache locality and loop blocking

children.objective: Explore an explicit register-tiled FP32 SIMD microkernel, using the ISA enabled for the supplied target; assess whether packing panels is worthwhile with its allocation and copy costs included. Keep this branch single-threaded to isolate kernel throughput. Handle arbitrary dimensions and edge tiles, overwrite all output elements, preserve the required FP32 tolerance for signed inputs, and measure both timed sizes with one thread.
children.subject: Explicit SIMD microkernel and panel packing

children.objective: Explore OpenMP scaling within the caller's thread budget using race-free ownership of output rows or tiles and an appropriate static partition. Keep this branch focused on parallel decomposition and avoid explicit ISA intrinsics or packing; use a generic cache-aware loop kernel as needed. Do not mutate global OpenMP settings or exceed the supplied threads value. Validate all supported sizes and measure both timed sizes with one and four threads, including any parallel overhead.
children.subject: OpenMP thread-budget scaling and output partitioning
